scope: Bounded static comparison of CPU and early-SoC support in official DS1522+ and DS1525+ firmware. Only decision-relevant family/package gates, V1500B power policy, selected CPU/memory/PSP modules, and AMD firmware directory entries were examined. No NAS access, target execution, firmware write, new infrastructure, or shared REA session mutation.

judgment.missing_cpu_prerequisite: No specific V1500B family/package, memory-training blob, microcode category, or SMU model-handling prerequisite missing from DS1522+ was identified.
judgment.positive_support: The actual family/package matcher and its candidate-construction block are byte-identical, all eight PMU code/data entries are byte-identical, three of four microcode entries are byte-identical, and both SMU DXE modules implement a V1500B configuration branch with a 16 W path.
judgment.not_established: Whole-stack compatibility, successful V1500B memory training on the DS1522 board, the failed chip's selected platform ID, or that peripheral topology is the only possible difference.
judgment.interpretation: The comparison supports continuing the concrete board-policy investigation. It does not establish a need to import a CPU-initialization component from DS1525, and does not by itself make a hardware swap or firmware deployment ready.

family_package_gate.semantics: The matcher reads CPUID leaf 0x80000001, compares EAX masked by 0x0fff0f00 with the supplied candidate, then compares EBX[31:28] with the candidate package byte. The common caller block constructs constants 0x00810f00, 0x00820f00, and 0x00810f80, each with package byte 0, and invokes the same matcher in the same branch sequence.
family_package_gate.establishes: For the same CPUID inputs these compared instruction blocks behave the same. The DS1525 support is not supplied by a distinct replacement family/package check at this gate.
family_package_gate.limit: These two blocks are not every CPU-related branch in either firmware. They do not observe the actual failed replacement chip's CPUID/package/fuse state.

ds1522.fact: An OPN string equal to V1500B selects 16000 mW for sustained, slow, and fast power limits and writes SystemConfiguration token 0x4f02b=2.

ds1525.fact: The V1500B match remains. When token 0x4f03e is nonzero AND SystemConfiguration token 0x4f02b is 3, it selects sustained/slow limits of 25000 mW and fast limit of 30000 mW, retaining token value 3. Otherwise it uses the same three 16000 mW limits and token value 2.

v1500b_power_policy.interpretation: This is an additional conditional power-policy option in DS1525, not evidence that DS1522 lacks V1500B recognition. The actual DS1525 runtime values of the enabling tokens were not observed, so this does not assert that DS1525 normally runs the higher-power branch.
v1500b_power_policy.limit: Executing either configuration branch on the user's replacement chip was not observed. Do not copy power settings based on this comparison.

module_inventory_comparison.pairing: Exact extracted filename, with PEI FFS GUID fragment included where present. Hashes cover full extracted PE bytes, including headers/relocations/data.
module_inventory_comparison.note: Most selected PE files differ. Some differences can include relocation/build data; full-file inequality alone is not a semantic CPU-support difference. No whole-stack equality is claimed.

amd_blob_comparison.method: Use previously retained PSPTool directory metadata, independently verify each directory magic in the source payload, hash the exact listed packed/signed entry extent, and pair the same directory/type/instance. Equality here means exact stored bytes, not version-label similarity.
amd_blob_comparison.changed_families: PSP boot/recovery loaders and trusted OS, all compared ABL0–7 entries, the SMU off-chip variants, and APCB defaults differ. ABL version labels are 21.2.12.EE versus 23.6.19.EE; PSP boot/OS labels are 0.8.A1.7D versus 0.8.A0.90.
amd_blob_comparison.microcode_detail: Both contain four listed microcode patches. IDs 0x8200103, 0x8108109 and 0x8108002 have identical bytes. The remaining slot differs: DS1522 contains 0x8101016, DS1525 contains 0x810100b. Patch applicability to the unobserved failed chip was not inferred from the patch IDs alone.
amd_blob_comparison.limit: Encrypted PSP contents and the behavioral consequences of changed AMD blob revisions were not reverse engineered. Presence of a changed revision does not identify a V1500B prerequisite missing from the other image.

remaining_difference.finding: This extracted module is absent by name from DS1522. No dependency tying it to first-time V1500B CPU initialization was established; its existence alone is not an identified missing-support blocker.

limits: DS1525 official V1500B operation validates its own motherboard and settings; it does not certify a DS1522 CPU replacement.

Official APCB bytes compared here are defaults. The main investigation reports live DS1522 APCB differences; this subtask did not read the live image and does not treat the default APCB comparison as complete current-configuration evidence.
Equal PMU programs do not prove equal SPD data, board memory parameters, signal integrity, or the outcome of training.
Different AGESA-related modules/blobs may include fixes beyond peripheral topology; no exact such missing prerequisite was identified within this bounded scope.

Deployment authenticity, preservation of live board data, recovery access, and useful failure diagnostics remain separate requirements owned by the main investigation. No recommendation to replace the CPU or flash a comparison-model image follows from this result.
tools: Python SHA-256 and exact PE/firmware byte comparison
